land.text: Pinsk, the semi-independent principality created within Turov after the succession of 1162

predecessors.note: The Turov-and-Pinsk dossier (eu-16-e) closes on 1293 and names this dossier as the Pinsk successor; Cliopatria's Pinsk row starts in 1294.

land.text: Pinsk, 'incorporated into the Grand Duchy of Lithuania' by 1320

successors.note: The Grand Duchy's dossier (eu-15) records the gain in 1326, the first year of Cliopatria's Lithuanian shape that holds Pinsk (145 of 145 cells); the Pinsk page says 'By 1320, Pinsk was incorporated'. Pinsk then 'remained ruled by local lines of the Gediminids' until 1521.

capitals.name: Pinsk
capitals.note: 'In 1241, the Orthodox diocese was moved from Turov to Pinsk.' The Turov page gives Turov as the capital of the whole principality and no separate capital for Pinsk; Pinsk is the seat of the appanage.

keyframe_review.note: 34,431 km2 (149 cells), 25.4-28.2 E, 51.0-53.5 N, round Pinsk and the Pripyat; the western half of the old Turov-Pinsk land (the Turov shape holds the eastern 125 cells). The Turov page gives only 'the territory of modern-day Belarus and northern Ukraine' and no area, and lists Pinsk among sub-principalities of Turov; the shape stands as Cliopatria's division.

correction.text: the same Pinsk land, 33,893 km2, valid 1314-1320; from 1320 it is Lithuanian ('By 1320, Pinsk was incorporated into the Grand Duchy of Lithuania')

keyframe_review.note: Four cells fewer than 1294 (145). The shape is right in extent but the page puts the incorporation into the Grand Duchy 'By 1320', not after 1325 as Cliopatria draws it (Cliopatria's Lithuanian shape takes the cells in 1326); the years 1321-1325 are left to the Grand Duchy and the eu-15 dossier still dates its gain 1326.

region.text: Pinsk, the appanage that split from Turov

ledger.note: 1294 (Cliopatria's first year): Pinsk appears as its own principality. The Turov page has 'A semi-independent Principality of Pinsk was created' after the 1162 succession and 'Principality of Pinsk (12th century - 16th century)' among the sub-principalities, without a year; it adds that by the early 14th century 'Hleb Narymunt, the son of Gediminas, was already ruler of Pinsk, while Turov and Haradok were still ruled by Rurikids'.

By 1320: Pinsk is incorporated into the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. 'By 1320, Pinsk was incorporated into the Grand Duchy of Lithuania' and 'It remained ruled by local lines of the Gediminids'; the same page has 'captured by Lithuanian duke Erdvilas' and 'Pinsk became a fief of Lithuania' without a year. The year is the page's upper bound; Cliopatria draws Pinsk as its own row to 1325.
The principality ends as an independent state and becomes a Gediminid fief of Lithuania (Narimantas, a son of Gediminas, 'ruled Pinsk and Polotsk' at various periods, Narimantas page, no dates).

wars.name: Pinsk against Lithuania
wars.outcome: 'In 1274, Pinsk along with Ruthenian princes and Tatars fought against Lithuania'; 'Afterwards, it was captured by Lithuanian duke Erdvilas, and Pinsk became a fief of Lithuania' and 'By 1320, Pinsk was incorporated into the Grand Duchy of Lithuania'.
wars.note: The page places the capture after 1274 without a year; zones are empty because it names no ground fought over. Reviewer (eu-16-f, 2026-10-31): 'from' moved from 1274 to 1294, the dossier's start, so the war lies inside the life; the 1274 fighting ('In 1274, Pinsk along with Ruthenian princes and Tatars fought against Lithuania', Pinsk page) belongs to the Turov-and-Pinsk years.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary; the Turov-Pinsk frontier and the marsh border with Galicia-Volhynia and Lithuania are approximate.

notes: THE TWO ROWS. Cliopatria's 'Principality of Pinsk' and 'Principality of Turov' (1294-1325) share Wikidata Q671362 with the earlier 'Principality of Turov and Pinsk' (1188-1240, dossier principality-of-turov-and-pinsk by eu-16-e, which ends in 1293 and hands over to both slugs). They are different states here: the Turov page has Pinsk 'created' as a semi-independent principality inside Turov, and in the early 14th century a Gediminid (Narymunt) ruled Pinsk while Rurikids still ruled Turov and Haradok; the two shapes touch but do not overlap (149 and 125 cells). So there are two dossiers, principality-of-pinsk and principality-of-turov; neither merges the other. END DATE CONFLICT. The Pinsk page says 'By 1320, Pinsk was incorporated into the Grand Duchy of Lithuania' (the eu-15 Grand Duchy dossier also cites the 1320 phrase for the western Rus principalities), but Cliopatria keeps the Pinsk row to 1325 and its Lithuanian shape takes Pinsk in 1326 and the eu-15 dossier dates its gain 1326. This dossier ends in 1320 on the page; 1321-1325 is therefore a five-year hole unless the Grand Duchy dossier moves its Pinsk gain to 1320 or this end is moved to 1325 (a gap-filler should decide). THIN PAGES: the Turov page names no year for any event of 1294-1325; the Narimantas page gives no year for Pinsk. Page budget: three pages (budget 1-2), one of them (Narimantas) silent on dates.
